items.title: Section: The Six Perfections as One — a Great White Ocean of Virtue, a Gushing Spring of Treasure

items.zh: 復次，如是六種波羅蜜多，世尊彼彼素怛纜中處處散說，今於此中攝在一處，略說應知。謂佛所說素怛纜中，所有施波羅蜜多乃至慧波羅蜜多，或標或釋，彼皆於此或自性施，廣說乃至或清淨施趣入攝受，如其所應皆當了知。如是所餘，如所宣說戒乃至慧趣入攝受，如其所應亦當了知。又諸如來為菩薩時，所行一切菩薩行中，所有無量本生相應難行苦行，當知一切與施相應，依止於施。如說其施，如是戒、忍、精進、靜慮、慧相應，依止戒、忍、精進、靜慮、慧，當知亦爾。或唯依施，廣說乃至或唯依慧，或雜依二，或雜依三，或雜依四，或雜依五、或雜依一切六波羅蜜多，皆應了知。如是六種波羅蜜多，菩薩為證無上正等菩提果故，精懃修集。是大白法溟，名大白法海；是一切有情、一切種類圓滿之因，名為涌施大寶泉池。又即如是所集無量福智資糧，更無餘果可共相稱，唯除無上正等菩提。
items.en: Furthermore, these six perfections, which the World-Honoured One taught scattered throughout many different discourses, are here gathered together into one place, and should be understood in this brief, unified form... The same holds for everything else, including what was taught concerning the four means of gathering beings — this too should be understood as drawn into this same framework, just as appropriate... A bodhisattva's practice may rely on generosity alone, or, in full detail, on wisdom alone, or on a mixture of two, three, four, five, or the complete set of all six perfections together — all of this should be understood. These six perfections, which bodhisattvas diligently cultivate in order to realise supreme, complete awakening, form a great, deep ocean of wholesome virtue; they are the single complete cause of every kind of being's fulfilment, a gushing spring of inexhaustible treasure. And the immeasurable accumulation of merit and wisdom they gather together is matched by no fruit whatsoever — except supreme, complete awakening itself.

items.zh: 云何菩薩四種攝事？嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，名略說攝事。謂九種相攝事，名為菩薩四種攝事。一者、自性攝事，二者、一切攝事，三者、難行攝事，四者、一切門攝事，五者、善士攝事，六者、一切種攝事，七者、遂求攝事，八者、此世他世樂攝事，九者、清淨攝事。

items.title: Section: Kind Speech Opens — Four Kinds of Words, Three Underlying Marks

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性愛語？謂諸菩薩，於諸有情常樂宣說悅可意語、諦語、法語、引攝義語。當知是名略說菩薩愛語自性。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's kind speech of intrinsic nature? Bodhisattvas constantly and genuinely delight in speaking to beings words that please, words that are simply true, words aligned with the dharma, and words that draw the listener towards real benefit. One should understand this, in brief, as a bodhisattva's own intrinsic nature of kind speech.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive Kind Speech — Genuine Greeting, Genuine Celebration, and the Full Etiquette of Meeting Someone Well

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切愛語？謂此愛語略有三種。一者、菩薩設慰喻語。由此語故，菩薩恒時對諸有情遠離顰蹙，先發善言，舒顏平視，含笑為先，或問安隱吉祥，或問諸界調適，或問晝夜怡樂，或命前進善來，以是等相慰問有情，隨世儀轉，順覩人性。二者、菩薩設慶悅語。由此語故，菩薩若見有情妻子、眷屬、財穀，其所昌盛而不自知，如應覺悟，以申慶悅。或知信、戒、聞、捨、慧增，亦復慶悅。三者、菩薩設勝益語。由此語故，菩薩宣說一切種德圓滿法教相應之語，利益安樂一切有情，恒常現前以勝益語而為饒益。是名菩薩一切愛語差別應知。云何略說如是菩薩一切愛語？當知此語略為二種。一、隨世儀軌語，二、順正法教語。若慰喻語、若慶悅語，當知是名隨世儀軌語；若勝益語，當知是名順正法教語。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive kind speech? This speech is, in brief, of three kinds. First, bodhisattvas offer comforting, greeting speech: through this speech, bodhisattvas constantly remain free of any furrowed brow towards beings, speak good words first, keep an open, level expression, lead with a genuine smile, and ask after another's wellbeing and good fortune, or the balance of their basic health, or whether their days and nights have passed pleasantly, or invite them warmly forward — comforting and greeting beings in all these ways, following ordinary worldly courtesy, attentive to each person's differing character. Second, bodhisattvas offer celebratory speech: seeing a being's spouse, family, or wealth genuinely flourishing, yet unaware of it themselves, bodhisattvas awaken them to it as appropriate and express genuine celebration; or, knowing that someone's faith, discipline, learning, generosity, or wisdom has genuinely grown, bodhisattvas likewise celebrate. Third, bodhisattvas offer beneficial teaching speech: through this speech, bodhisattvas proclaim words aligned with the complete, perfect teaching embodying every kind of virtue, genuinely benefiting and bringing ease to every being, constantly and presently offering real benefit through this speech. These should be understood as a bodhisattva's comprehensive kind speech in its distinct forms. How, in brief, may this comprehensive kind speech be described? One should know this speech is, in brief, of two kinds: first, speech following worldly courtesy; second, speech aligned with the true teaching. Both comforting speech and celebratory speech should be understood as speech following worldly courtesy; beneficial teaching speech should be understood as speech aligned with the true teaching.

items.title: Section: Difficult-Practice Kind Speech — Comforting an Enemy, Patiently Teaching the Slow, and Kindness Towards the Deceitful

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行愛語？當知此語略有三種。若諸菩薩，於能殺害怨家惡友，以善淨心、無穢濁心，思擇為說若慰喻語、若慶悅語、若勝益語，當知是名菩薩第一難行愛語。若諸菩薩，於其上品愚癡鈍根諸有情所，心無疑慮，思擇為說種種法教，誓受疲勞，如理如法，如善攝取，當知是名菩薩第二難行愛語。若諸菩薩，於其諂詐欺誑親教、軌範、尊長真實福田行邪惡行諸有情所，無嫌恨心、無恚惱心，思擇為說若慰喻語、若慶悅語、若勝益語，當知是名菩薩第三難行愛語。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's difficult-practice kind speech? One should know this speech is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who, towards an enemy or evil friend capable of killing them, still speak with a genuinely good and pure mind, entirely free of any hidden defilement, deliberately choosing to offer comforting speech, celebratory speech, or beneficial teaching speech — this is called a bodhisattva's first difficult-practice kind speech. Bodhisattvas who, towards beings of the most extreme delusion and dullest faculties, harbour no doubt or hesitation at all, deliberately choosing to teach them the various forms of the dharma, willingly accepting the exhaustion this requires, correctly and lawfully, genuinely gathering them in — this is called a bodhisattva's second difficult-practice kind speech. Bodhisattvas who, towards beings who deceive and flatter their own genuine teachers, mentors, and worthy elders through wrongful conduct, harbour no resentment and no hostility at all, deliberately choosing to offer comforting speech, celebratory speech, or beneficial teaching speech nonetheless — this is called a bodhisattva's third difficult-practice kind speech.

blocks.text: The six perfections gathered into one, then the second means of embracing beings: kind speech. A short passage (0529c16) is untranslated.

"These six perfections, which the World-Honoured One taught scattered through many discourses, are here gathered into one place", "a great ocean of virtue". Master Cháng Bǎi: the four means of embracing are "the rest" that follows.

"Words that please, words that are true, words aligned with the Dharma, and words that draw towards benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: they correspond to avoiding harsh speech, lies, divisive speech, and idle talk.

**Greeting**: "free of any furrowed brow", an open face and a smile before speaking (Master Cháng Bǎi: so the person feels welcome). **Celebrating** others' good fortune. **Speech of supreme benefit**: teaching the Dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng reads one phrase as following the habits of courteous people.

Towards "an enemy or evil friend capable of killing them", still speaking kindly; towards "beings of the most extreme dullness", patiently teaching (Master Cháng Bǎi: if they don't listen once, say it a hundred times; if not after a hundred, a thousand); and towards those who deceive their own teachers.
Speech is where practice meets other people every day. The treatise asks for something simple and hard: an open face, a greeting first, words that are true and kind.

quiz.q: In §22, the English reads "the rest" as including the four means of embracing. How do the two lectures read "suǒ yú"?
options: Cháng Bǎi per the 《披尋記》: the four means; Miào Jìng: discipline through wisdom — calling the 《披尋記》's reading a poor fit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the four means of embracing are "the rest." Venerable Miào Jìng: "the rest" is discipline through wisdom as described before; the 《披尋記》's reading does not fit the text. The English follows the former.

quiz.q: What four kinds of words make up a bodhisattva's intrinsic kind speech?
options: pleasing words, true words, dharma words, words drawing towards benefit
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas constantly delight in speaking to beings words that please, words that are true, words aligned with the dharma, and words that draw the listener towards real benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: kind speech has these four contents and three marks.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi say commentators match the four kinds of kind speech to the four verbal precepts?
options: Jing and Ce: pleasing = no harsh speech, true = no lying, dharma = no divisive speech, beneficial = no idle talk; Kuiji differs; and each may contain all four
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Jing and Ce say pleasing words are non-harsh speech, true words non-lying, dharma words non-divisive, beneficial words non-idle; Kuiji pairs them differently; and one need not pair them — each contains all four kinds of good speech.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of comprehensive kind speech?
options: comforting words, celebratory words, words of supreme benefit
quiz.why: "First, bodhisattvas offer comforting, greeting speech … second, celebratory speech … third, speech of supreme benefit." Venerable Miào Jìng: "shè" here means learning — the bodhisattva must learn comforting speech.

quiz.q: Comforting speech: "free of frowning, speaking good words first, open expression, smiling first." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: an open, smiling face — smiling before speaking — so the person feels welcome
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a bodhisattva speaking with others must not frown — open the face, smile before speaking, so the person feels welcome. Venerable Miào Jìng: "level gaze" means looking neither up nor down.

quiz.q: Who are the three recipients of difficult kind speech?
options: an enemy capable of killing one; the extremely dull; those who deceive their teachers and true fields of merit
quiz.why: Towards an enemy able to kill; towards beings of the most extreme dullness; towards those who deceive their preceptors, teachers, and elders — true fields of merit. Venerable Miào Jìng: "true fields of merit" are noble ones.

quiz.q: Towards the extremely dull, "vowing to bear the fatigue" — what do the lectures say?
options: if one time doesn't work, tell them a hundred times, then a thousand — tirelessly; Miào Jìng: "vow" means resolve, unafraid of hardship
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if they don't listen once, say it a hundred times; if not after a hundred, a thousand — teaching patiently. Venerable Miào Jìng: "vow" means resolve — able to bear the fatigue of teaching them, unafraid of hardship.
